evidence_packet.title: Ofsted suspends four Manchester nurseries after boy dies
evidence_packet.lead: Four Cosy Toes Ltd nurseries have been temporarily closed after the death of 3-year-old Thiago Wall
evidence_packet.summary: Four Cosy Toes Ltd nurseries have been temporarily closed after the death of 3-year-old Thiago Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Ofsted suspends four Manchester nurseries after boy dies - BBC News Image caption, The boy became critically ill at Cosy Toes Nursery in Middleton shortly before 16:00 GMT on Monday 2 November By Georgie Docker North West Published 19 November 2026 Four nurseries in Greater Manchester have been temporarily closed after the death of a three-year-old boy. Cosy Toes Nursery, in Middleton, was suspended from Ofsted's childcare register on 3 November after Thiago Wall became critically ill there on 2 November and died three days later. Ofsted has since confirmed it has also suspended the registrations of three other Middleton nurseries run by Cosy Toes Nursery Ltd. Boarshaw Private Day Nursery, Kirkway Nursery and Twinkle Toes Nursery were removed from the register on 5 November. Greater Manchester Police confirmed on Wednesday that it had launched an investigation into the death of the three-year-old boy. The force said: "As the circumstances leading up to the boy's death occurred in a care setting, and in line with usual procedure, a police investigation has been opened. No arrests have been made at this time." The boy's family is being supported by specialist officers, police added. An Ofsted spokesperson said: "Our thoughts are with the family of the young boy and everyone affected by this deeply distressing and tragic incident. "We have worked closely with the police and have suspended the nursery's registration. "We will continue to support the police and other agencies in their enquiries." The watchdog said it was unable to comment further while the police investigation was ongoing. Under Ofsted guidance, suspensions from the early years register are initially imposed for six weeks, but can be ended sooner or extended if necessary. According to the government website

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Westside Cowboy named BBC Introducing Artist of the Year 2026 - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The band have become known for their energetic live performances and interwoven four-part harmonies By Lauren Hirst North West Published 19 November 2026 Westside Cowboy have been announced as BBC Introducing Artist of the Year 2026. Jimmy Bradbury, Reuben Haycocks, Aoife Anson O'Connell and Paddy Murphy formed the band in Manchester in 2023 and have since rocketed from the pub circuit to some of the UK's biggest festivals. The award is presented to an up-and-coming artist or band who has, with the support of BBC Introducing, made a significant impact and has previously been won by Olivia Dean, Myles Smith and Tom Grennan. Murphy, from Longridge in Lancashire, said the win put them in "good company", with Bradbury, from Shropshire, adding that it was "very flattering". BBC Introducing supports new musical talent across the UK , providing a platform to propel new artists on to the local and national stage through 30 Introducing shows, three national radio shows and six shows across BBC Radio 1, Radio 1Xtra, Radio 2, 6Music, Radio 3 and Asian Network. About 72,000 tracks from emerging UK artists supported by BBC Introducing make it on to the airwaves each year. Westside Cowboy uploaded their debut single I've Never Met Anyone I Thought I Could Really Love (Until I Met You) to the Introducing platform in November 2024 and had their first play on radio within hours. Image caption, Murphy and Bradbury were surprised with the award during a radio interview The four-piece played in various other bands before coming together to form Westside Cowboy. evidence_packet.title: Tameside homes evacuated after explosives found in house
evidence_packet.lead: An 83-year-old man says he did not even have time to pack a bag before leaving his Droylsden home
evidence_packet.summary: An 83-year-old man says he did not even have time to pack a bag before leaving his Droylsden home
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An 83-year-old man who was ordered from his home after the bomb squad found ammunition and explosives at a nearby house has said he did not even have time to pack his bags Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said officers had been called to an "unrelated investigation" in Shelley Grove, Droylsden, on Wednesday afternoon when the discovery was made, leading to the evacuation A cordon was put in place while an explosive ordnance disposal unit worked to make the area safe Officers arrested a man in his 20s on suspicion of criminal damage, arson and possession of ammunition. A man in his 70s and a woman in her 60s were held on suspicion of unlawfully possessing ammunition and explosive substances The cordon remained in place at 12:40 GMT and a GMP spokesperson said it was not yet known when it would be lifted Brian Ridsdale said he was at home watching television when firefighters knocked on his front door and told him to leave

title: Graves of missing North West soldiers found in Belgium and France

evidence_packet.title: Graves of missing North West soldiers found in Belgium and France
evidence_packet.lead: Lieutenant Fred Naylor, of Aspull, and Company Sgt Major Herbert Bannister, of Wavertree, died in 1918
evidence_packet.summary: Lieutenant Fred Naylor, of Aspull, and Company Sgt Major Herbert Bannister, of Wavertree, died in 1918
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The graves of two lost World War One soldiers from the north-west of England have been found in Belgium and France more than a century after their deaths Lieutenant Fred Naylor from Aspull, in Wigan, and Company Sergeant Major Herbert Bannister, of Wavertree, Liverpool, died in March and April 1918 and were both named on memorials to the missing Naylor was first identified as "unknown soldier" by badges on his uniform, the Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC) said Ministry of Defence (MOD) case worker Alexia Clark said: "Working on cases where there is a chance to reunite a man with his name is always special." The research was carried out by the MOD, the National Army Museum and CWGC CWGC case worker Polly Brewster said: "We are honoured to have played a role in the identification of their final resting places."

title: Dambusters raid survivor visits home of Lancaster bomber

evidence_packet.title: Dambusters raid survivor visits home of Lancaster bomber
evidence_packet.lead: Christa Chadwick was nine when the Dambusters raid took place in Germany during World War Two
evidence_packet.summary: Christa Chadwick was nine when the Dambusters raid took place in Germany during World War Two
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman who survived the Dambusters raid during World War Two has climbed into the cockpit of a replica Lancaster bomber used in the famous mission Christa Chadwick was nine when RAF 617 Squadron flew over Germany's Ruhr Valley in an operation to breach three dams on the night of 16 and 17 May 1943 She recalled: "People were running around through the streets screaming, 'Das wasser kommt' [the water is coming] Chadwick, from Knutsford, Cheshire, stepped inside a replica of a bomber during a visit to the Avro Heritage Museum in Woodford, Stockport The museum is located at the site of the former Woodford Aerodrome where famous aircraft, including the Lancaster bomber, were built About 1,300 people were killed in the flooding that followed the bombing of Möhne dam and the Eder dam

title: Failings contributed to Walkden arson attack deaths, family tells inquest

evidence_packet.title: Failings contributed to Walkden arson attack deaths, family tells inquest
evidence_packet.lead: The family of a woman who was murdered, along with her four children, say police failed to intervene
evidence_packet.summary: The family of a woman who was murdered, along with her four children, say police failed to intervene
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The family of a mother who was murdered in an arson attack along with her four youngest children have said failings by police and local authorities contributed to their deaths, an inquest heard Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move before the murders Final submissions from lawyers for the family, Greater Manchester Police and others were heard earlier. GMP said the evidence did not support that their inaction had probably caused or contributed to the deaths The murders came after a feud involving mother-of-six Michelle's eldest son Zak Bolland, 26, his accomplice David Worrall, 28, and Bolland's girlfriend, Courtney Brierley, 20, were all jailed over the fatal attack in December 2017

evidence_packet.lead: Shabir Ahmed, 73, was released from prison in July after 14 years behind bars
evidence_packet.summary: Shabir Ahmed, 73, was released from prison in July after 14 years behind bars
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government is still considering "every option" to deport Rochdale grooming gang leader Shabir Ahmed, a Home Office minister has said, months after ministers suggested emergency legislation could be used to remove him from the UK Ahmed, 73, was released from prison in July after serving 14 years for rape and other sexual offences against girls, some as young as 12 The government said at the time that it would seek to deport Ahmed to Pakistan. Having been stripped of his British citizenship, he now holds only Pakistani nationality However, he remains in the UK because existing legislation prevents the deportation of some Commonwealth citizens A minister said earlier that officials were "determined" to remove him from the country Lord Collins of Highbury was asked in the House of Lords whether the Home Office had threatened Pakistan with the withdrawal of foreign aid or visa sanctions

title: Graves of missing North West soldiers found in Belgium and France

evidence_packet.title: Graves of missing North West soldiers found in Belgium and France
evidence_packet.lead: The graves of two lost World War One soldiers from the north-west of England have been found in Belgium and France more than a century after their deaths Lieutenant Fred Naylor from Aspull, in Wigan, and Company Sergeant Major Herbert Bannister, of Wavertree, Liverpool, died in M
evidence_packet.summary: The graves of two lost World War One soldiers from the north-west of England have been found in Belgium and France more than a century after their deaths Lieutenant Fred Naylor from Aspull, in Wigan, and Company Sergeant Major Herbert Bannister, of Wavertree, Liverpool, died in M
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The graves of two lost World War One soldiers from the north-west of England have been found in Belgium and France more than a century after their deaths Lieutenant Fred Naylor from Aspull, in Wigan, and Company Sergeant Major Herbert Bannister, of Wavertree, Liverpool, died in March and April 1918 and were both named on memorials to the missing Naylor was first identified as "unknown soldier" by badges on his uniform, the Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC) said Ministry of Defence (MOD) case worker Alexia Clark said: "Working on cases where there is a chance to reunite a man with his name is always special." The research was carried out by the MOD, the National Army Museum and CWGC CWGC case worker Polly Brewster said: "We are honoured to have played a role in the identification of their final resting places."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman who survived the Dambusters raid during World War Two has climbed into the cockpit of a replica Lancaster bomber used in the famous mission Christa Chadwick was nine when RAF 617 Squadron flew over Germany's Ruhr Valley in an operation to breach three dams on the night of 16 and 17 May 1943 She recalled: "People were running around through the streets screaming, 'Das wasser kommt' [the water is coming] Chadwick, from Knutsford, Cheshire, stepped inside a replica of a bomber during a visit to the Avro Heritage Museum in Woodford, Stockport The museum is located at the site of the former Woodford Aerodrome where famous aircraft, including the Lancaster bomber, were built About 1,300 people were killed in the flooding that followed the bombing of Möhne dam and the Eder dam

evidence_packet.lead: The family of a mother who was murdered in an arson attack along with her four youngest children have said failings by police and local authorities contributed to their deaths, an inquest heard Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was fi

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The family of a mother who was murdered in an arson attack along with her four youngest children have said failings by police and local authorities contributed to their deaths, an inquest heard Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move before the murders Final submissions from lawyers for the family, Greater Manchester Police and others were heard earlier. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mystery medal belonging to a soldier who was killed in World War One is set to be handed over to his family Joyce Smith found the medal, assigned to Pte Joseph Newbury, from The Sherwood Foresters (Nottinghamshire and Derbyshire Regiment), among her late husband's collection at her home in Bolton and appealed for help to find relatives of the soldier Andy Bye, an amateur family historian, got in touch and tracked down the great granddaughters of Pte Newbury, from Derby, after finding his military records The granddaughters are now planning to meet Smith, who will give them the medal to keep Amanda Reed, 60, from Bramhall in Greater Manchester, said it was kind of Bye to carry out the research into her great grandfather, who died in September 1915 "What a lovely thing of Andy to do, to go to all that trouble, to find the family, basically, of people that he doesn't even know," she said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Greater Manchester station named as Britain's quietest railway station The station gets just two services a week Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 17:41, 19 Nov 2026 Reddish South station (Image: Jason Robe A Greater Manchester station has been named as Britain's quietest station of last year with less than a hundred 'entries and exits' recorded over a 12-month period Just 94 entries and exits - meaning the number of times passengers start or end a journey at a particular station - were recorded at Reddish South Station in the year to the end of March 2026 That figure is down from 102 entries and exits recorded the previous year, according to new figures released by the Office of Rail and Road It sits on the Stockport-Stalybridge line, which only sees two train services per week - with one Saturday morning service in both directions Denton station also sits on the same line and has similar 'ghost' status, recording just 54 entries and exits between April 2023 and March 2024. Bomb disposal experts were also called to the scene following the discovery at the property A cordon was put in place and residents were evacuated from their homes. Greater Manchester Police said officers attended the address at 2.22pm to make an arrest attempt as part of an ongoing and unrelated investigation A force spokesperson said: "Emergency services attended the scene, and officers recovered ammunition and discovered potentially hazardous substances. Officers said a man in his 20s has been arrested on suspicion of criminal damage, arson, and possession of ammunition. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A business does not need to stand beside a river to face a flood risk. During heavy rain, water can collect where it cannot soak into the ground or drain away quickly enough, affecting entrances, loading areas and routes across a site. For businesses in Greater Manchester, the us Surface-water flooding occurs when rainwater remains on the ground or flows over it rather than entering drainage systems or soaking into the soil. That makes it different from flooding caused by a river overtopping its banks: a site some distance from a watercourse can still be For a business, the first visible problem may be water across a delivery route rather than inside the building. A low point at a vehicle entrance can affect access, while standing water near an external doorway may make it harder to move people or stock safely. These are reasons The Environment Agency’s guidance to the Risk of Flooding from Surface Water Map explains how to use mapped risk as an initial indication of where flooding may occur. Its scenarios include events with annual probabilities of 3.3%, 1% and 0.1%. Those figures describe the chance of A map cannot establish exactly what will happen at an individual building. Modelling at area scale may not capture every kerb, threshold, private drainage feature or change made to a site, and a mapped boundary should not be read as a precise line of safety. A manager can use it The next step is a walk around the parts of the site that matter most to safe access and continued operation. evidence_packet.summary: on WhatsApp Share via Email The Government is to end its use of Altrincham's Cresta Court Hotel as accommodation for asylum seekers, more than two years after its sudden closure to the public sparked widespread controversy Altrincham and Sale West MP Connor Rand confirmed today t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email The Government is to end its use of Altrincham's Cresta Court Hotel as accommodation for asylum seekers, more than two years after its sudden closure to the public sparked widespread controversy Altrincham and Sale West MP Connor Rand confirmed today that the remaining asylum seekers will leave the Church Street hotel "over the next few months" The decision follows the closure of the Britannia Ashley Hotel in Hale as asylum accommodation in August and paves the way for the potential return of one of Altrincham's best-known hotels to its former use The announcement marks the beginning of the end of one of the most contentious issues in Altrincham in recent years and raises the prospect of one of the town's best-known hotels returning to commercial use It was on October 29th 2024 that Altrincham Today confirmed that the Cresta Court had been closed to house asylum seekers , having broken the news of its sudden closure the previous evening The 148-bedroom hotel, a fixture of Altrincham's hospitality scene since the 1970s, had shut with immediate effect, leaving customers with existing bookings for weddings, Christmas parties and other events facing last-minute cancellations

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man who drugged and raped his wife for more than 20 years wanted a stranger to abuse her in a hotel room while he filmed it, a court has heard The husband pleaded guilty in September to multiple offences from 2004 onwards including rape, sexual assault and administering a substance with intent to commit a sexual offence He will give evidence later this month against nine men on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court over their alleged roles in the abuse The man, who is in his 60s and cannot be identified to protect his wife's anonymity, took images and videos of his offending at their home in Stockport, Greater Manchester, while she was "out of it", and then shared them online The prosecution says that from 2023 at the latest, he began inviting other men to the address, where, it is claimed, they too sexually abused her On Thursday, prosecutors continued to outline the timeline of the husband's communications with the defendants and other un-named individuals

evidence_packet.title: Failings contributed to Walkden arson attack deaths, family tells inquest
evidence_packet.lead: Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move b
evidence_packet.summary: Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move b
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move before the murders Final submissions from lawyers for the family, Greater Manchester Police and others were heard earlier. GMP said the evidence did not support that their inaction had probably caused or contributed to the deaths The murders came after a feud involving mother-of-six Michelle's eldest son Zak Bolland, 26, his accomplice David Worrall, 28, and Bolland's girlfriend, Courtney Brierley, 20, were all jailed over the fatal attack in December 2017 Anna Morris KC, representing the Pearson family, said the ultimate culpability for the "heinous murders" was with the three perpetrators

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Council has invested more than £30m in neighbourhood services funding cleaner streets, improved parks and green spaces, stronger action on fly-tipping and better-maintained highways The investment is already delivering results, including improved street cleansing standards and upgrades to local infrastructure across the city The enhanced programme, which had been funding improvements since 2023, has resulted in 1,340km of roads being cleansed across the city and improved standards for cycle lanes, contributing to a 24.7% reduction in formal street cleansing complaints over the last year Significant improvements have also been made to waste collection services. Additional investment has also helped improve fly-tipping clearance on Council l The Council continues to take robust action against environmental offences. evidence_packet.summary: Manchester City Council can announce that Portland Street will be reopened to traffic from the early hours of Wednesday morning (November 4)
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Council can announce that Portland Street will be reopened to traffic from the early hours of Wednesday morning (November 4) This follows an extensive programme of emergency repairs due to a broken water main which ruptured last week A large-scale operation was put into action to isolate the source of the leak and repair it, and then carry out a full repair and resurface of the damaged road Crews from United Utilities and the Council have worked around the clock since Friday afternoon to ensure that the road could be reopened as quickly and safely as possible. This has been alongside TfGM staff who have also put additional resource into redirecting affected public t Illustrating the scale of the repairs needed, roughly 600 tonnes of road surface has been planed away and replaced over the course of these works The restrictions on the road are planned to be removed early on Wednesday morning (November 4), with the road practicably useable to motorists shortly after that

title: £270,000 funding boost for playgrounds in Failsworth

evidence_packet.title: £270,000 funding boost for playgrounds in Failsworth
evidence_packet.lead: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund
evidence_packet.summary: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The seafood and cocktail bar and Champagne-led tasting menu restaurant have both caught the attention of Michelin’s inspectors… Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Two more Manchester restaurants have been added to the Michelin Guide, with Bar Shrimp and Portfolio both making the cut in its November update The two city centre spots are markedly different propositions, but both are the work of teams already well acquainted with the Michelin Guide Part seafood restaurant, part cocktail bar and part late-night music spot, Bar Shrimp brings together the team’s collective obsessions with sustainably sourced seafood, great drinks and records With its David Lynch-inspired red velvet interiors and Mastersounds sound system, the bar serves everything from oysters and caviar to smoked fish croquettes, alongside an inventive cocktail list Its next-door sister restaurant, Higher Ground, was added to the Michelin Guide in September 2023, just seven months after opening, going on to secure a Bib Gourmand in January 2024

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Mauricio Pochettino hit the nail on the head with 'most important' part of Manchester United job Mauricio Pochettino has conducted his first sit-down interview with club media as Man Utd head coach and he said some interesting things. Add to pr "The culture, to create the culture is the most important. To have the culture is the most important." Mauricio Pochettino was unequivocal about the most important part of his job as the new Manchester United head coach. To the layman, it might look like winning games and dragging the club clear of relegation trouble should be the top priority, but the 54-year-old knows all of tha Pochettino is a builder. In his best job, at Tottenham, he created a culture and a philosophy to drive the team and the club forward. There is an argument to say this is exactly what he needs to do now that he is in charge at Old Trafford Later on in his MUTV interview, Pochettino spoke of him and his staff needing "to adapt to the culture of the club." evidence_packet.summary: Приготовьтесь к незабываемому вечеру с одной из самых любимых звезд турецкой поп-сцены — Муратом Далкылычем, в Лондоне! После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки

После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он приобрел большую и преданную аудиторию как в Турции, так и за ее пределами. 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне. Вас ждет яркий вечер турецкой поп-музыки, живого исполнения и любимых хитов. Не упустите возможность увидеть Мурата Далкылыча вживую в Лондоне! Предварительный заказ
